Technique pure : confiner le roi et le m: Pure technique: confine the king and mate without stalemate.
Carré, opposition, cases clés, triangula: Square, opposition, key squares, triangulation, corresponding squares, outside or protected passed pawn, races. Every move is checked by calculation.
Lucena, Philidor, Vancura, puis la règle: Lucena, Philidor, Vancura, then Tarrasch's rule, the short side, the cut-off king, the active rook. Judged by the Syzygy tables.
Dame contre pion sur la 7e (central, de: Queen against a pawn on the 7th (central, bishop, rook) and queen against rook.
Cavalier ou Fou contre pion, Fou contre: Knight or bishop against pawn, bishop against knight, opposite-coloured bishops: win with the right piece, draw with less material.
Tour et Fou contre Tour : la position de: Rook and bishop against rook: the Philidor position (win) and the Cochrane defence (draw).
Gardez la Dame à un saut de cavalier du: Keep the queen a knight's jump from the enemy king: it takes away the most squares without being approachable.
Rétrécissez la zone pas à pas, puis amen: Shrink the zone step by step, then bring your king in support (opposition at two squares).
Avant chaque coup : le roi adverse garde: Before each move: does the enemy king still have a free square? If not, it's stalemate.
Dame + Roi contre Roi se gagne toujours: Queen + king against king always wins in about ten moves. Confine the king to an edge with the queen (a knight's jump away), advance your king to the opposition, then mate. The only trap: stalemate.
Coupez le roi adverse avec la Tour sur u: Cut off the enemy king with the rook on a rank or file, far from it (it must never be able to capture it).
Méthode de la boîte : à chaque coup de T: Box method: with each rook move shrinking the zone, advance your king to support it.
Quand les rois sont en opposition (une c: When the kings are in opposition (one square between them), a rook check pushes the king toward the edge.
La technique de la « boîte » : la Tour d: The “box” technique: the rook marks the escape zone, the king approaches, and each opposition allows a check that shrinks the box to the edge. Theoretical maximum: 16 moves.
Les deux Tours se relaient : l'une coupe: The two rooks take turns: one cuts a rank, the other checks on the next rank.
Si le roi adverse s'approche d'une Tour,: If the enemy king approaches a rook, move it to the other end of its rank, without leaving it en prise.
Le « mat de l'escalier » : les deux Tour: The “ladder mate”: the two rooks climb in turn one rank at a time and push the king to the edge, where one mates while the other cuts the next rank. The attacking king isn't even needed.
Côte à côte, les deux Fous forment une b: Side by side, the two bishops form a barrier of neighbouring diagonals the enemy king can't cross.
Rapprochez votre roi et réduisez la zone: Bring your king closer and reduce the zone toward a corner, never leaving the enemy king without a free square out of check: that would be stalemate.
Deux Fous matent toujours, en vingt coup: Two bishops always mate, in twenty moves at most. Placed side by side, they bar two neighbouring diagonals; the strong king comes to support them, and the enemy king is pushed to a corner, any corner, where mate falls.
